old: The server is granted for up to 120 days and every resource is returned to the pool at expiry, so the recurring cost is a fresh registration rather than a renewal click; the vendor states the period may change.
new: The server is granted for up to 120 days in two steps, 60 days and then a further 60 days, and the user must extend it at the 60-day mark after a reminder email.

evidence.proved: IBM's overview deck for the self-service virtual server states the trial is 60 + 60 days, up to 120, extended by the user at the 60-day mark after a reminder email
evidence.quote: Students are responsible for extending to 120 days at the 60 day mark. They will get an email reminding them.

reason: IBM's own overview deck gives the 120-day term as 60 days plus a 60-day extension the user requests from a reminder email, and the portal ships an entitlement-extension page, so 'a fresh registration rather than a renewal click' is contradicted; the expiry clearing stays in limits[0] with the terms as its source

evidence.proved: the terms still state a term of up to 120 days, after which all resources are cleared of data and returned to the pool
evidence.quote: Access to the LinuxONE Community Cloud is for up to 120 days, as further determined by the use and subject to change as agreed by IBM and you.

evidence.proved: IBM's overview deck lists the public virtual-server trial as 60 days plus 60 days, up to 120 days
at the end of the term the server's resources are cleared of data and returned to the pool
evidence.quote: Once such period has expired, all resources will be cleared of your data (if applicable) and returned to the pool at Marist University’s discretion.

evidence.proved: the portal's extension controller posts a token from the link to /cloud/user/api/service/extend and reports a successful entitlement extension
evidence.quote: Thank you!  Your entitlement on the LinuxONE Community Cloud has been extended successfully.
